```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 07_sampling_variability
title: >
  Which poll would surprise you more?
questions:
  - id: poll_size_prediction
    type: free-response
    checkLabel: Compare your answer
    prompt: >
      Imagine two polls drawn at random from our evenly split population. One
      asks 12 people, the other asks 1,200. Which would surprise you more if
      three-quarters of its respondents supported Candidate Left? Why?
      Try reasoning it out without calculating a probability.
    answer: >
      The poll of 1,200. In a small sample, a few people can tip the proportion
      a long way from 50/50. We'd expect a larger sample to come closer to the
      population's even split, so a result of 75% would be more surprising.
    explanation: >
      Neither result is impossible. The question is how much room chance has
      to produce a lop-sided result when the population itself is evenly split.
```
